Vendored official TrivialAugment augmentation library (also provides the RandAugment sampler)
=============================================================================================

Paper (TA)   : S. G. Müller, F. Hutter. "TrivialAugment: Tuning-free Yet State-of-the-Art Data
               Augmentation". ICCV 2021. arXiv:2103.10158
Paper (RA)   : E. D. Cubuk, B. Zoph, J. Shlens, Q. V. Le. "RandAugment: Practical automated data
               augmentation with a reduced search space". NeurIPS 2020. arXiv:1909.13719
Repository   : https://github.com/automl/trivialaugment   (official, by the TA author)
Commit       : e6545d80affcc18b7024185a096e93e21010023e  (master, 2023-03-07)
File         : aug_lib.py
License      : MIT (vendor/LICENSE, copied from the same commit)

Why this file and not a reimplementation
  * The TA README: "we recommend to simply copy over the file aug_lib.py to your codebase".
  * It is the code path that produced the TA paper's CIFAR-100 WRN-28-10 numbers
    (TrivialAugment/augmentations.py::get_randaugment -> aug_lib.UniAugmentWeighted / aug_lib.RandAugment).
  * RandAugment has no official PyTorch implementation (official code is TF1 graph code in
    tensorflow/tpu, ImageNet-only). aug_lib.RandAugment is the sampler the TA authors used to
    reproduce RandAugment on CIFAR-100 WRN-28-10 with the paper's N=2, M=14
    (confs/wresnet28x10_cifar100_b128_maxlr.1_randaug_fixedsesp_200epochs_2_nowarmup.yaml).

Files
  aug_lib_official.py.orig   byte-for-byte copy of the official file
                             sha256 8f5f9febb671fd12be067e311dbdcb837a2a29c672861f20c2cf03732fdd2868
  aug_lib.py                 the imported copy
                             sha256 c25d9b858309487d6fcc54a8d8ec4d848f268c1deafecdeba7260d75a2a752f3

The ONLY change (line 9), required to import on Python >= 3.11:
  - @dataclass
  + @dataclass(frozen=True)  # [py3.11-patch] only change vs. official; see SOURCE.txt
  Python 3.11 rejects the unhashable MinMax(...) instances used as dataclass field defaults in
  MinMaxVals ("mutable default ... is not allowed"). Freezing MinMax makes it hashable. MinMax
  objects are never mutated anywhere in aug_lib.py, so sampling, ranges and op behaviour are
  unchanged. sanity_test.py asserts the diff against the .orig file is exactly this line.
